name: Opus 5 pairs
strategy: A single same-industry relative-value pair built on a company-specific guidance divergence - long UAL / short AAL in airlines at 15% per side (30% gross) - with the steel pair closed and 70% in cash at 4%.
reassessment_note: Research done this week by web search (finviz, SEC/IR-linked releases, earnings calendars). The steel pair was built on STLD guiding ahead of NUE; that divergence has broken. On 10-19 STLD reported Q3 adj EPS $5.26, below consensus (~$5.48) and below its own September guide of $5.34-5.38, on lower selling prices, narrower metal spreads, and aluminum yield problems (the stock fell ~5.8% premarket before recovering to roughly my entry). NUE guided Q3 to $5.55-5.65 and reports after the close on Monday 10-26, the exact close at which this book enters, so holding the pair would mean owning an earnings binary with no researched edge in either direction. The pair is down about 2.5 spread points; I am closing both legs to cash rather than flipping it into the print. The airline pair stays. UAL's 10-20 report was weak on guidance: Q3 adj EPS $2.54 vs ~$2.58 consensus, and Q4 guided to $0.50-1.50 vs ~$1.80 consensus on $4.80/gal jet fuel, which caps the full year near $7.22 vs July's $9-11. The UAL leg is -11%, and that is the main source of the book's -1.22% NAV. But the shock is industry-wide fuel, which a long/short airline pair is built to net out, and UAL still printed a record $17.9B revenue with unit revenue up ~16% and remains solidly profitable. AAL guided to a Q3 loss and a full year straddling zero. AAL reported on 10-22; I could not find coverage of its print, so I am relying on its July guidance plus the tape (AAL is down 5.6% from my short entry). Cutting gross from 70% to 30% is a deliberate de-risking while the remaining pair works through the fuel shock. Because re-registering resets the entry fills, I have re-set the stops so they sit near the original price levels instead of widening the risk.

positions.thesis: Long leg of the airline quality-spread pair. UAL's Q3 still produced record revenue ($17.9B, +17% YoY) and ~16% unit-revenue growth with adj EPS of $2.54. Its Q4 guide of $0.50-1.50 is a fuel story ($4.80/gal assumed, about $1/share of quarterly drag), and the AAL short hedges that fuel exposure. UAL keeps positive earnings through a fuel spike that pushes AAL to around breakeven or losses, which is the divergence the pair harvests. Held at an unchanged 15% after the guide cut. The 10% stop from roughly $98 (~$88) keeps the stop level close to the original -20%-from-$110 stop, so I am not adding risk to a leg that is already down.

Short leg and fuel hedge for the UAL long. AAL is the most levered and least profitable of the big three: it guided Q3 to an adj loss of $0.10-0.70 and the full year to -$0.65 to +$0.65, and in September its CFO flagged Q4 fuel running about $1/gal above the July assumption (~$1B of added cost). With a weaker balance sheet and less premium/international mix, it has less ability than UAL to pass fuel through in fares. The short is +5.6% since entry. I could not find coverage of its 10-22 Q3 print, so the leg rests on its guidance and the tape. Sized to match UAL at 15% so fuel and sector beta net out. The 25% stop (~$15.1 from a ~$12.1 entry) sits near the original stop level of ~$15.4.
